title: Ang 1203–1230: Guru Arjan's Sarang
hookLine: the fifth Guru's many midday hymns
tomorrow: whose mother, whose father? why would a Guru ask that?

cards: The message is typed. Half of it's in capitals. Your thumb is hovering over send, your face is hot, and every word in it is true.
That's the moment the hymn is for. From ang 1203, Guru Arjan's Sarang hymns run page after page, and in one of them he gives the Name a temperature. Not bright.

teach.b: In paraphrase, the hymn says: the way of the Lord's Name is cool. Seekers searched the old scriptures and the holy people, and drew it out.

Thaandhee, the word is: cool, the way shade is cool at noon, the way a wet cloth is cool on a hot forehead. Put that in the middle of a fight. Anger runs hot; that's not a metaphor anyone has to explain.
The Granth doesn't tell you the heat is fake, or that you have no reason.
It offers a different temperature to stand in. And notice where this sits: in Sarang, the midday raga, where the sun is highest. The hymn knows exactly how hot it gets.
Something to tell a friend tonight: you can't argue someone out of being overheated, but you can hand them something cool first, and then talk. The order matters. Cool, then words.
Guru Arjan's Sarang keeps returning the mind to the Name, and in this hymn, the Name is the shade you step into before you speak.

how: Ragis sing Guru Arjan's Sarang hymns in kirtan; some Sikhs repeat Waheguru or a line of Gurbani under their breath to steady themselves when anger flares.

games.q: your brother borrowed your car and brought it back on empty, again. you're typing in capitals. what does Guru Arjan's 'cool' hymn point you to?
o: put the phone down, cool off, then say it plainly.
send it now while it's honest; cooling down is just hiding.
say nothing, ever; peace means never bringing it up.
games.why: the hymn calls the Name's way cool. it doesn't silence what's true; it changes the temperature you say it in.

practice: Close your eyes. With each breath out, let a little heat leave: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands. Don't chase the thought you're angry about; just let the temperature drop, one breath at a time.
If you pray, you can let the Name ride the breath out. If you'd like, read ang 1204 before you begin.
